title: Kohayakawa–Nagle–Parczyk conjecture on squares of Hamilton cycles in random graphs
statement:
Let $G(n,p)$ be the binomial random graph on vertex set $[n]$, with each possible edge included independently with probability $p=p(n)$. A square of a Hamilton cycle is the second power of a Hamilton cycle: for some cyclic ordering of the vertices, every pair of vertices at cyclic distance at most two is an edge. **Kohayakawa–Nagle–Parczyk conjecture.** For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if

$$
p\geq (1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{e/n},
$$

then $G(n,p)$ a.a.s. contains a square of a Hamilton cycle. This is a more precise proposed sufficient condition than the earlier threshold prediction; the supplied passage does not state whether it has been resolved.
source_name: Yulin Chang, Jie Han and Lin Sun, “The threshold for powers of tight Hamilton cycles in random hypergraphs”, arXiv:2310.18980 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18980

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).
